plan: To preserve capital, we will sell all leveraged ETFs (METU, SOXL, MUU, MSFU, PLTU, SPAL) to zero.
This eliminates the highest-risk components of your portfolio.
QQQI will be trimmed to 20% to meet the single-name concentration mandate.
This strategy prioritizes stability and reduces overall portfolio volatility.
conservative.read: This conservative plan aims for capital preservation with a target of ~1.5% per month. It significantly de-risks the portfolio by eliminating leveraged ETFs and reducing concentration. Expect lower volatility and smaller drawdowns, but also more modest growth potential.

plan: For balanced growth, we will trim all leveraged ETFs (METU, SOXL, MUU, MSFU, PLTU, SPAL) to smaller allocations.
This reduces overall leverage while maintaining some exposure to growth sectors.
QQQI will be trimmed to 25% to meet the single-name concentration mandate.
A new position in OXY will be initiated at 4% based on its strong scanner read, diversifying the portfolio.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets ~2.5% per month by blending broad index exposure with quality tech and a small amount of leverage. It aims for risk-first growth, reducing overall portfolio risk while still seeking upside. Expect moderate volatility and drawdowns.

plan: For aggressive growth, we will add to existing leveraged ETFs (METU, SOXL, MUU, MSFU, PLTU, SPAL) to increase exposure.
QQQI will be trimmed to 25% to meet the single-name concentration mandate.
A new position in OXY will be initiated at 6% based on its strong scanner read.
This strategy leans into leverage and concentration in high-scoring setups for maximum growth potential.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4% per month by stretching growth through increased leverage and concentration. This approach significantly raises both upside potential and drawdown risk. Leveraged ETFs decay daily, and this strategy can lead to substantial losses quickly if not managed with strict stop discipline.

plan: To prioritize income, we will sell all leveraged ETFs (METU, SOXL, MUU, MSFU, PLTU, SPAL) to zero.
This eliminates high-beta and leveraged positions that do not align with an income focus.
QQQI will be increased to 30% to enhance monthly distributions, while respecting the mandate.
This strategy aims for steady income and lower drawdown, treating the portfolio as cash-like.
income.read: This income plan targets ~1% per month by rotating into income-focused ETFs and broad index exposure. It prioritizes low drawdown and reliable distributions over growth. While aiming for steady income, distributions are variable and NAV can still fall in a selloff; this is not a savings account.
